items.question: Against what reference should completeness of a Claude output be evaluated?

options.A: The length and detail level of a typical response to a similar question.
options.B: The specific requirements or brief the output was intended to address.
options.C: The volume of information available in the context window.
options.D: The acceptance threshold established for similar outputs in prior review cycles.

items.question:
A 400-person specialty insurance firm uses Claude.ai for drafting client correspondence. Their operations manager hears the phrase "Claude API" from a vendor and asks what it means in plain terms.

Which description BEST captures what the Claude API is?

options.A: A programmatic interface that lets software applications send instructions to Claude and receive responses without a human manually typing into a chat window.
options.B: A premium tier of Claude.ai that unlocks longer conversation history and higher file upload limits for enterprise subscribers.
options.C: A set of configuration settings inside Claude.ai that lets administrators define company-wide defaults for tone and output format.
options.D: A cloud storage service that holds documents so Claude can reference them consistently across multiple chat sessions.

items.question:
A retail chain's digital marketing manager needs to update product descriptions for 8,000 SKUs. She currently pastes each item one at a time into Claude.ai.

What is the PRIMARY indicator that her workflow has outgrown the chat interface?

options.A: She needs descriptions that are more accurate than what Claude can produce within a single chat session's context limit.
options.B: The task involves a high volume of identical operations that must run without a human triggering each one individually.
options.C: Claude.ai does not support the spreadsheet format she uses to manage SKU data.
options.D: She needs to share the generated descriptions with three other team members simultaneously.

items.question:
A 12-person fintech startup is building its first Claude API integration. The lead analyst asks why "tokens" keep appearing in cost discussions.

Which explanation MOST accurately describes a token in this context?

options.A: A security credential that authenticates each API request to prevent unauthorised access.
options.B: A unique call identifier assigned per API request for billing reconciliation and audit logging.
options.C: A small chunk of text—roughly three to four characters on average—that the model uses as its basic unit for reading input and generating output.
options.D: A pre-purchased bundle of credits the company acquires in advance before making API calls.

items.question:
A global pharma company's regulatory affairs team uses the API to review draft clinical-trial summaries. Their manager assumed that only the length of Claude's response affects API costs.

Which statement CORRECTLY describes how token costs are calculated?

options.A: Costs are based solely on the number of output tokens Claude generates, because reading input is a passive operation.
options.B: Costs are based on total session length in minutes, with a per-minute rate that applies regardless of token volume.
options.C: Costs are based only on input token count, because output generation is a fixed-cost operation charged as a flat fee per call.
options.D: Costs are based on both the input tokens sent to the model and the output tokens returned, with each direction contributing to the total billed amount.

items.question:
A 15,000-employee logistics company uses Claude.ai for ad hoc queries. A supply chain analyst is asked to evaluate whether a proposed daily report pipeline should use the API instead. The pipeline would run overnight, apply the same structured prompt to updated shipment data, and output results into the company's dashboard system.

Which TWO characteristics of the proposed workflow most strongly indicate that the API is the right choice? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The reports will occasionally contain sensitive supplier data that should not pass through a consumer chat product.
options.B: The pipeline must run on a fixed overnight schedule without any human initiating each individual run.
options.C: The reports will be reviewed by a manager before distribution, providing a human checkpoint.
options.D: The same structured prompt will be sent to Claude many times per day with only the input data varying between calls.
options.E: The output format requires markdown rendering that the dashboard system handles natively.

items.question:
A large hospital system's clinical documentation specialist is evaluating whether Claude can summarise a patient's longitudinal record spanning 14 years of notes, totalling roughly 280 pages. The engineering team mentions "context window" as a potential constraint.

What does the term "context window" refer to in this scenario?

options.A: The maximum amount of text—measured in tokens—that Claude can hold in active memory for a single request, encompassing both the input sent and the output it generates.
options.B: The number of previous conversation turns Claude retains between separate sessions when the same document is re-opened.
options.C: A configurable parameter that limits how many pages of a document the API processes per call, adjustable by the IT administrator.
options.D: The display panel in Claude.ai where both the uploaded file and the model's response are visible to the user simultaneously.

items.question:
A strategy consultant loads a 90-page due-diligence report into an API call and asks Claude to produce a 40-page executive summary. The API returns an error indicating the request exceeded the model's output limit. The consultant has verified the input document fits within the context window.

What is the MOST likely cause of this failure?

options.A: The source document is too large for the context window, and the error message is being misreported by the API client.
options.B: The requested output length exceeds the model's separate maximum output length, which is a distinct ceiling from the context window.
options.C: The model requires the document to be split into sub-sections before it can generate any continuous output.
options.D: Claude's content filters blocked output for documents containing commercially sensitive merger information.

items.question:
An insurance company's IT architect is designing an API-based triage system to classify 50,000 incoming claim emails per day. All emails arrive within a two-hour window each morning.

Which design concern does this traffic pattern introduce that must be addressed before go-live?

options.A: The model will degrade in classification accuracy when processing a large number of similar tasks in rapid succession.
options.B: Each API call will require a separate authentication challenge, creating overhead proportional to call volume.
options.C: Sending the full volume within a two-hour window may exceed the API tier's rate limit, causing requests to be throttled or rejected.
options.D: The system will need to pre-fetch and cache all emails locally before the API can begin processing them.

items.question:
An automotive manufacturer's process automation team deployed a Claude API integration six months ago to generate quality-inspection summaries. Last week the team updated their configuration to track the provider's "latest" model alias. Two days later, QA flagged that summaries now follow a different structure than the templates downstream systems expect.

What is the MOST likely root cause?

options.A: The API key was automatically rotated after six months and the new key was issued for a different account tier.
options.B: The prompt template is too brief to enforce output structure, so any model would produce varied results over time.
options.C: The provider's content-safety policy was updated, causing new filters to reformat the summaries.
options.D: The "latest" alias resolved to a newly released model version whose output behaviour and default formatting differ from the version the integration was built and tested against.

items.question:
A 200-attorney law firm's legal operations manager is working with a developer to build a client-facing contract-review tool via the API. The developer asks which requirements should be encoded in the system prompt rather than left to individual user requests.

Which TWO items belong in the system prompt? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The instruction that Claude should always flag indemnification clauses as requiring partner review before client delivery.
options.B: The specific contract document being reviewed in the current session.
options.C: The requirement that Claude respond only to contract-law questions and redirect off-topic requests.
options.D: The governing jurisdiction relevant to the specific contract submitted by the user.
options.E: The user's preferred output language, selected at login and stored in the user's profile.

items.question:
A non-profit's grants director has been using Claude.ai to help draft proposals. She is told that the API would allow her team to "build something more powerful." She asks her IT volunteer what kind of user or team the API is designed for.

Who is the INTENDED primary audience for the Claude API?

options.A: Developers and technical teams who want to integrate Claude's capabilities into applications, automated pipelines, or products they are building.
options.B: Enterprise subscribers who pay for the highest Claude.ai plan and receive direct API access as part of their subscription benefit.
options.C: Researchers who need to query Claude beyond the standard message limits without being interrupted by usage caps.
options.D: Non-technical users who need to bypass the Claude.ai interface due to corporate firewall restrictions on web-based tools.

items.question:
A media company's content operations lead runs a team that manually pastes 300 article headlines per week into Claude.ai for SEO scoring. She is exploring ways to eliminate the manual effort.

Which aspect of this process is the CLEAREST signal that it is a poor long-term fit for the chat interface?

options.A: The SEO scores need to be reviewed by an editor before they are acted upon.
options.B: The same repetitive action is performed hundreds of times weekly, making human-triggered chat impractical and error-prone at that volume.
options.C: The headline outputs need to be stored in a content management database for later analysis.
options.D: The headlines contain editorial strategy information that should not be typed into a browser-based interface.

items.question:
A large retailer's e-commerce director is reviewing a monthly API cost report that came in higher than budgeted. The engineering team confirms the average API call contains a 2,000-token system prompt, a 500-token product description, and a 200-token output.

Where is the LARGEST single cost contributor per API call in this configuration?

options.A: The 200-token output, because generating text is more computationally expensive per token than reading input.
options.B: The 500-token product description, because variable inputs are billed at a higher rate than fixed overhead components.
options.C: The 2,000-token system prompt, because it is re-sent on every API call and represents the largest token count in each request.
options.D: The API connection overhead metadata, which typically exceeds the content tokens for short requests.

items.question:
An institutional research analyst at a 40,000-student university is building an API integration to auto-generate standardised statistical summaries from enrollment reports. She asks her developer what the "temperature" parameter controls.

Which description MOST accurately explains temperature in this context?

options.A: The computational priority level assigned to a request, where lower temperature means the request is processed faster.
options.B: A safety threshold that determines how sensitive the model is to potentially restricted topics in the input.
options.C: The maximum token length of the response, with higher temperature permitting longer outputs.
options.D: A parameter that controls the randomness of the model's output, with lower values producing more deterministic and consistent responses.

items.question:
A utility company's regulatory compliance officer is designing an API workflow that will pass a 200-page regulatory filing to Claude and ask it to generate a 50-page compliance summary. The engineering team flags two separate concerns that could each independently cause the workflow to fail.

Which TWO distinct technical constraints could each independently prevent this workflow from succeeding? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The API does not accept PDF inputs; the document must be converted to plain text before submission.
options.B: The 200-page filing may exceed the model's context window, preventing the full document from being loaded in a single request.
options.C: Claude cannot produce output that is longer than the input it received.
options.D: The compliance domain may trigger content-safety restrictions that block regulatory text from being processed.
options.E: The requested 50-page summary may exceed the model's maximum output length per call.

items.question:
A 25-person digital health startup is building a patient-facing symptom-checker app. The product manager assumes they can use Claude.ai's web interface as the backend for the app's AI features, embedded via a web view.

Why is this approach NOT viable for their product?

options.A: Claude.ai is a consumer product designed for human users, not a callable endpoint. Building a product requires API access so the app's code can send and receive requests programmatically.
options.B: Claude.ai does not permit healthcare-related queries due to liability restrictions imposed by Anthropic.
options.C: The startup would need to purchase an enterprise Claude.ai plan and receive written approval before any commercial application is permitted.
options.D: Claude.ai sessions are limited to one concurrent user, making it unsuitable for a multi-user application.

items.question:
A global telecoms company's digital transformation lead is planning a customer-churn prediction workflow that will send 100,000 customer records to Claude for analysis over a 4-hour batch window. The engineering team is on a standard API tier.

What should the transformation lead raise with the engineering team BEFORE the integration goes live?

options.A: Whether Claude's churn-prediction accuracy meets the statistical threshold required to justify the business case.
options.B: Whether the standard tier's rate limits can sustain the required throughput within the 4-hour window, and whether a tier upgrade or request-spreading strategy is needed.
options.C: Whether the API supports bulk file upload so the 100,000 records can be submitted in a single call.
options.D: Whether the model version currently in use is the same one that was used during the accuracy evaluation.

items.question:
A bid manager at a 500-person consulting firm is troubleshooting an API integration that generates proposal sections from a large RFP. The call consistently errors when she requests a 15,000-word output. She has confirmed that the RFP document fits within the context window.

What should she do NEXT to isolate the cause of the failure?

options.A: Reduce the RFP document size by half to rule out a context window overflow that the error message may be misreporting.
options.B: Switch to a higher-tier model, which supports a larger context window and can therefore generate longer outputs.
options.C: Test whether requesting a much shorter output from the same input succeeds, confirming that maximum output length—not the context window—is the binding constraint.
options.D: Add an explicit instruction in the system prompt telling Claude to ignore output length restrictions for business-critical proposal work.

items.question:
A bank's compliance officer is reviewing the architecture of a Claude API integration used by loan officers. She wants to ensure that specific risk-disclosure language is included in every response regardless of what individual officers ask.

Which mechanism provides the MOST reliable way to enforce this requirement?

options.A: Training the loan officers to always include the required disclosure language in their own requests to Claude.
options.B: Post-processing every API response with a script that appends the disclosure text before the response reaches the officer.
options.C: Storing the required disclosure in a Project knowledge document that Claude can reference when asked.
options.D: Encoding the disclosure requirement in the API system prompt, which the application sets and which applies to every call without any action from individual users.

items.question:
A precision-parts manufacturer uses an API integration to generate non-conformance reports. The engineering team is debating whether to pin a specific model version or always use the "latest" alias.

Which TWO risks does tracking "latest" introduce that pinning a specific version avoids? (Choose TWO)

options.A: A new model version may produce output in a different format, breaking downstream parsing logic built for the previous version's structure.
options.B: The provider may discontinue the API entirely when releasing a new model version, leaving the integration without a backend.
options.C: Rate limits and per-token pricing may change with each new model version, causing unpredictable billing.
options.D: Output behaviour, tone, or reasoning style may shift in a new version, requiring re-validation of the integration's accuracy before the change can be accepted.
options.E: The API authentication method changes with each new model release, requiring credential updates on every version transition.

items.question:
An insurance firm's actuarial analyst notices that API costs are running 40% over budget. A review reveals the system prompt is 3,500 tokens, including a 1,200-token company history section that is not relevant to the rating tasks Claude performs.

What action would MOST directly reduce per-call token costs?

options.A: Remove the irrelevant 1,200-token company history from the system prompt, reducing input token count on every single API call.
options.B: Switch to a higher-tier model that processes tokens more efficiently and therefore costs less per token for the same task.
options.C: Reduce temperature to zero, which causes the model to generate shorter responses and therefore fewer output tokens.
options.D: Consolidate multiple API calls into single longer calls to benefit from bulk-processing cost efficiencies.

items.question:
A government agency's policy analyst has deployed an API integration that classifies incoming public comments into regulatory categories. Different team members report receiving different classifications for identical comment text, which is causing inconsistencies in the audit trail.

What API-level setting should the integration team adjust FIRST to reduce this output variability?

options.A: Increase the context window allocation to ensure the full comment text is included in every request without truncation.
options.B: Set temperature to its lowest value, minimising randomness and making the model's output consistent for the same input.
options.C: Add a post-classification validation layer that runs each comment twice and picks the most common result.
options.D: Switch to a lower-tier model, which produces more deterministic outputs by default compared to higher-tier models.

items.question:
A 20-person retail startup's growth analyst is building an API integration to generate 500-word product stories for 3,000 catalogue items. The CFO asks for a pre-launch cost estimate before committing budget.

Which approach gives the MOST reliable pre-launch cost estimate?

options.A: Multiply the number of SKUs by the context window size to estimate maximum possible cost.
options.B: Run the integration on 10 items and use the exact average output token count from those runs to project full cost.
options.C: Run a representative sample of 50–100 items, record the actual input and output token counts, and extrapolate based on the observed distribution.
options.D: Assume each 500-word output equals 500 tokens, multiply by the per-token output price, and add a fixed overhead per call.

items.question:
A university's academic operations analyst manually copies 150 course-feedback surveys per week into Claude.ai for sentiment analysis. He asks his supervisor whether this process is a candidate for API automation.

What is the CLEAREST signal that this workflow should migrate to the API?

options.A: The sentiment analysis outputs need to be stored in the institution's learning management system.
options.B: The feedback forms contain student names that should not be entered into a consumer chat interface.
options.C: The analyst sometimes receives inconsistent sentiment ratings for similar survey responses.
options.D: The process consists of a repetitive, predictable-cadence task that requires no human judgement per item and runs at a volume that makes manual initiation disproportionately costly.

items.question:
A global consulting firm's knowledge management director is deploying an internal research assistant via the API for 5,000 consultants. She wants consistent behaviour across all users.

Which THREE capabilities can the system prompt reliably provide? (Choose THREE)

options.A: Preventing the model from ever acknowledging that it is an AI system, regardless of how directly a user asks.
options.B: Setting a consistent communication style—such as concise and structured—that applies to every interaction.
options.C: Restricting the assistant's scope to research questions and redirecting requests for legal or financial advice.
options.D: Guaranteeing that the assistant will never refuse any request submitted by an authorised consultant.
options.E: Specifying the output format—such as numbered lists or executive-summary headings—for all responses.

items.question:
A broadcaster's data engineering team builds an API pipeline to process a backlog of 20,000 archived articles. They submit all 20,000 requests simultaneously in the first minute. The pipeline fails with rate-limit errors after approximately 600 articles.

What change would MOST directly resolve this failure?

options.A: Introduce request pacing so that the call rate stays within the API tier's requests-per-minute limit throughout the processing run.
options.B: Upgrade to the highest available model tier, which carries a higher rate limit by default.
options.C: Split the 20,000 articles across four separate API keys to distribute the load across multiple limits.
options.D: Reduce the average input length per article to consume fewer tokens per call and lower the effective load.

items.question:
A pharma company's clinical data manager wants to send 180 pages of cross-trial study reports to Claude in a single API request for synthesis. Her developer estimates the combined document is near the model's context window limit.

What is the PRIMARY risk of operating very close to the context window boundary?

options.A: The model will reject the request unless the documents are provided in a structured XML format.
options.B: As input approaches the context limit, the space available for the generated output shrinks, potentially truncating the synthesis or requiring a shorter response than needed.
options.C: The model prioritises the most recently read sections due to a first-in, first-out processing constraint that discards early content.
options.D: API latency increases exponentially when requests approach the context window limit, making the integration impractical for time-sensitive work.

items.question:
A bank's risk officer is reviewing an AI governance framework for a customer-communication API integration. An internal auditor asks what controls ensure the model's behaviour is consistent over time for regulatory examination.

Which control BEST addresses the auditor's concern?

options.A: Logging all API responses for 90 days and sampling them monthly for quality review.
options.B: Routing all API calls through a human review queue before customer delivery.
options.C: Pinning the integration to a specific model version so that regulatory review, testing, and production all operate on identical model behaviour, with any version change treated as a formal change event.
options.D: Storing the system prompt in a version-controlled repository so prompt changes are auditable.

items.question:
A 15-person logistics startup's founder is comparing the cost of Claude.ai Pro subscriptions for her operations team versus building an API-based automation. The team's Claude usage is light and irregular—a few sessions per week.

For LIGHT, IRREGULAR use, which cost argument generally favours the chat interface over the API?

options.A: The chat interface provides more favourable per-token pricing than the API for small workloads.
options.B: The API charges a fixed monthly minimum regardless of usage, making it expensive for low-volume teams.
options.C: Building and maintaining an API integration requires engineering investment that would outweigh token savings for irregular, human-driven use.
options.D: A flat-fee subscription is more cost-predictable and often cheaper for irregular human-driven use than paying per token consumed across unpredictable sessions.

items.question:
A mid-size clinic's IT director is briefing clinical staff on what parameters the development team has available when building their patient-triage API integration. Staff are asking whether AI behaviour can be controlled reliably.

Which TWO parameters are genuine API-level controls that directly shape model behaviour? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The system prompt, which establishes baseline instructions, persona, and constraints applied before every user message.
options.B: The training data filter, which can be configured to exclude clinical edge cases that confuse the model.
options.C: The response cache, which stores prior answers and returns them verbatim to ensure identical outputs for repeat inputs.
options.D: The temperature setting, which controls how deterministic or varied the model's outputs are for a given input.
options.E: The latency budget parameter, which tells the model to prioritise speed over quality when a response time threshold is exceeded.

items.question:
A telecoms company's product director wants to add a Claude-powered virtual assistant directly inside their mobile app so customers never leave the app to access AI support.

Why does this use case require the API rather than Claude.ai?

options.A: The API lets the telecoms company's application call Claude programmatically and display responses within their own interface, whereas Claude.ai is a standalone product users must visit directly.
options.B: The API is required because mobile apps cannot load Claude.ai in a web view for security reasons.
options.C: Claude.ai only supports desktop browsers, making it unusable for a mobile-native experience.
options.D: The API provides dedicated compute with lower latency than Claude.ai, which is necessary for a real-time chat experience in a mobile app.

items.question:
A retailer's digital product manager learns that their API integration sends a 1,500-token system prompt, a 400-token conversation history, a 300-token retrieved knowledge document, and a 100-token user question on each call.

Which elements contribute to the input token count billed on each call?

options.A: Only the 100-token user question, because the system prompt and knowledge documents are pre-loaded infrastructure not billed per call.
options.B: All four components—system prompt, conversation history, retrieved document, and user question—because everything included in the request body is counted as input tokens.
options.C: Only the system prompt and user question, because conversation history and retrieved documents are treated as ephemeral and not billed.
options.D: Only the user question and retrieved document, because those are the variable components that change between calls.

items.question:
A global insurer's solutions architect is designing an automated underwriting workflow. Underwriters submit policy applications throughout the day, and the workflow must guarantee a response within 30 seconds. The API tier used has a ceiling of 200 requests per minute.

Which design pattern BEST accommodates the rate limit while preserving the latency requirement?

options.A: Batch all incoming applications at the end of each hour and send them together in a single large API call.
options.B: Add a retry loop that immediately re-sends any rate-limited request until it succeeds.
options.C: Implement a queue with a rate-controlled dispatcher that holds new requests when the per-minute limit is near, and alerts if queue depth suggests the latency target is at risk.
options.D: Deploy multiple application instances, each using its own API key, to multiply the effective rate limit.

items.question:
A biotech startup's data analyst uses the API to extract structured data fields from laboratory reports. She notices the same report sometimes yields slightly different field values on re-runs. Her developer asks what parameter to adjust to make outputs more consistent.

What change should the developer make?

options.A: Increase the maximum output token limit to give the model more room to be thorough in its extraction.
options.B: Add a chain-of-thought instruction so the model shows its reasoning before committing to each extracted value.
options.C: Reduce the context window allocation to focus the model only on the relevant section of the report.
options.D: Set temperature to a low value, reducing randomness and making the model's extraction consistent across repeated runs of the same input.

items.question:
A city council's digital transformation manager is evaluating whether to give caseworkers Claude.ai Pro accounts or build a custom API integration for a document-classification task.

Which TWO advantages does a custom API integration offer that Claude.ai does NOT? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The ability to upload PDF documents for Claude to analyse.
options.B: Access to a more capable model tier than is available on any Claude.ai plan.
options.C: Programmatic control over output format, ensuring classifications are always returned in the exact structure the council's case management system requires.
options.D: Faster response times due to dedicated compute infrastructure that Claude.ai users share.
options.E: Automated batch processing that sends documents to Claude without a caseworker triggering each one manually.

items.question:
A wealth management firm's compliance analyst asks whether a carefully written system prompt can completely prevent users of an internal API tool from receiving inaccurate information from Claude.

Which statement MOST accurately reflects the relationship between a system prompt and factual accuracy?

options.A: A system prompt can constrain behaviour, tone, and scope, but it cannot guarantee factual accuracy—the model may still produce inaccurate content despite strong instructions.
options.B: A system prompt with an explicit "no hallucination" instruction prevents the model from generating unverified claims.
options.C: Factual accuracy is determined solely by the model tier; the system prompt affects style and scope but has no bearing on accuracy.
options.D: Setting temperature to zero combined with a strong system prompt eliminates factual errors for well-established financial domains.

items.question:
A law firm associate is reviewing an API integration that analyses 500-page merger-agreement packages. The integration sometimes produces summaries that omit provisions from the first hundred pages of the document.

What is the MOST likely technical explanation for this omission?

options.A: Claude processes documents with a first-in, first-out constraint, and the first hundred pages are overwritten as later pages are read.
options.B: When a very long document fills most of the context window, content near the beginning may receive less attention in the model's output than content near the end—a characteristic of long-context processing.
options.C: The integration's chunking algorithm splits the document at a boundary that excludes the first hundred pages from the context window.
options.D: The system prompt instruction to "summarise key provisions" is ambiguous and causes the model to focus on provisions with precedent cross-references rather than early structural clauses.

items.question:
An insurance CTO is choosing between two API tiers. Tier X has lower per-token pricing but a rate limit that can only sustain 60% of peak traffic before throttling. Tier Y costs 35% more per token but its rate limit comfortably handles 150% of peak traffic. The integration serves real-time claims processing under a contractual 30-second SLA.

What consideration should be MOST DECISIVE in this tier selection?

options.A: The lower per-token cost of Tier X will produce overall savings that outweigh occasional SLA breaches during peak periods.
options.B: The integration should be designed to handle throttling gracefully via retries, making the rate limit difference inconsequential for SLA compliance.
options.C: Tier selection should be deferred until real production traffic data is available, making either option premature at this stage.
options.D: For an integration with a contractual latency SLA, the rate limit's ability to sustain peak load without throttling is a hard constraint—the higher per-token cost is the price of SLA compliance.

items.question:
A media company's editorial director is reviewing an API cost-reduction initiative. Her team sends long article drafts with extensive revision history appended for context, and receives long structured feedback reports.

Which THREE changes would each independently reduce the token cost per API call? (Choose THREE)

options.A: Remove revision history from the context when it is not relevant to the current editorial feedback task.
options.B: Instruct Claude to return feedback in a concise bullet format rather than long narrative paragraphs.
options.C: Switch to a lower temperature setting, which reduces the computational cost of each token generated.
options.D: Shorten the system prompt by removing boilerplate instructions not needed for the editorial feedback task.
options.E: Request that Claude batch multiple articles in a single API call to benefit from economies of scale.

items.question:
A utility company's regulatory affairs director needs Claude to cross-reference a 350-page environmental impact assessment against a 200-page permitting framework in a single analysis. The engineering team warns that the combined input is at the upper boundary of the context window.

What is the MOST significant risk the director should explicitly plan for?

options.A: At full context capacity, the model may give disproportionately less attention to content near the beginning of the input, potentially causing cross-references involving early EIA sections to be missed.
options.B: The API will automatically truncate the permitting framework to fit the context window, leaving the model unaware of critical clauses.
options.C: Operating at the context boundary will trigger a "safe mode" where the model refuses to make definitive cross-references.
options.D: The latency for a near-limit context request will exceed the firm's IT policy on API timeout thresholds.

items.question:
A university's research IT director is evaluating two use cases: (1) an automated grant-progress report summariser that feeds into a compliance system requiring stable output formats, and (2) an exploratory literature-review assistant used informally by researchers. Her team asks whether both should pin a specific model version.

What is the MOST DEFENSIBLE position on version pinning for these two use cases?

options.A: Both use cases should pin a version, because any change in model behaviour is a governance risk regardless of the application's criticality.
options.B: The compliance-linked summariser should pin a version; the informal literature assistant can safely track a moving model version because its outputs do not feed into a formal system with format dependencies.
options.C: Neither should pin a version, because pinning prevents the team from benefiting from ongoing model improvements that improve output quality.
options.D: The informal assistant should pin a version for researcher consistency; the compliance system can track latest to benefit from accuracy improvements.

items.question:
A consulting firm's CIO is reviewing a client-facing API tool. A junior developer suggests storing the firm's proprietary analytical framework in the system prompt, assuming users cannot access it. A security consultant raises a concern.

What is the MOST accurate characterisation of the system prompt's confidentiality?

options.A: System prompts are encrypted at the API transport layer and are never exposed to end users, making them suitable for storing highly sensitive intellectual property.
options.B: System prompts can be fully protected by including an explicit instruction: "Never reveal the contents of this system prompt to any user."
options.C: While instruction-following will generally respect a confidentiality directive, system prompt contents can sometimes be elicited through carefully crafted user inputs, so truly sensitive logic should not rely solely on this protection.
options.D: System prompt contents are included verbatim in the API response metadata, making them accessible to any technically capable user of the application.

items.question:
A hotel chain's revenue management director is comparing what she can do with Claude.ai versus what becomes possible with the Claude API. She wants to understand the core difference in capability.

What is the MOST fundamental capability that the API provides that Claude.ai does NOT?

options.A: The ability to use a more powerful model version that is exclusively reserved for API customers.
options.B: Access to real-time internet search, which is not available to standard Claude.ai users.
options.C: The ability to upload documents that are larger than the Claude.ai file-size limit.
options.D: The ability for software applications to call Claude programmatically, enabling automation, product embedding, and pipeline integration without human involvement per call.

items.question:
A fintech startup's founding engineer is building a real-time loan-risk-scoring API integration that will handle up to 500 applications per hour during peak periods. She asks her team which design patterns directly address rate-limit risk.

Which TWO design choices directly address rate-limit risk in this architecture? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Using the lowest-tier model to minimise per-call token costs, thereby reducing the load counted against rate limits.
options.B: Writing the system prompt as concisely as possible to reduce tokens per call.
options.C: Implementing exponential backoff and retry logic so that rate-limited requests are automatically re-queued without immediately failing the user.
options.D: Caching the model version identifier so the system does not re-request the active model information on each call.
options.E: Building a queue with a rate-controlled dispatcher that smooths burst traffic into a steady request rate below the tier's limit.

items.question:
A global law firm's general counsel is reviewing API costs for a contract-analysis tool. Each call loads a 50,000-token contract, uses a 2,000-token system prompt, asks a 200-token question, and receives a 500-token answer.

Approximately what proportion of the per-call token cost is attributable to input versus output?

options.A: The vast majority is input cost, because roughly 52,200 tokens of input are sent for every 500 tokens of output.
options.B: The split is roughly equal, because input and output tokens are billed at the same rate.
options.C: Output tokens dominate because generation requires more compute than reading, reflected in a significantly higher per-token rate for output.
options.D: The 2,000-token system prompt is billed separately at a flat rate and does not factor into the input/output comparison.

items.question:
A non-profit program director notices her team spends 10 hours per week copying grant-disbursement data into Claude.ai to generate narrative reports for 40 local grantees. Her IT partner asks what single indicator most clearly signals that the API should replace the current approach.

What is THAT indicator?

options.A: The reports contain beneficiary data that violates the non-profit's data-handling policies when entered through a consumer chat product.
options.B: The process is repetitive, high-volume relative to its value, and performs the same prompt 40 times weekly—making manual initiation disproportionately costly.
options.C: Output quality is inconsistent because different team members phrase prompts slightly differently each week.
options.D: The reports need to be stored in the grants management system, which Claude.ai cannot write to directly.

items.question:
A hotel's guest experience manager is working with a developer to build an AI concierge via the API. She wants the assistant to always introduce itself as "Max" and to decline questions about competitor hotels.

Where do these behavioural rules belong in the API request?

options.A: In the user message on each API call, so the instructions are fresh and explicitly present for every interaction.
options.B: In the API request headers as custom metadata flags that the model reads before generating a response.
options.C: In the system prompt, which the application sets once and which applies before every user message, establishing Max's persona and scope for the entire session.
options.D: In a post-processing filter that replaces the assistant's name and strips any mention of competitor hotels from responses.

items.question:
A pharmaceutical company's medical affairs manager is building an API tool to answer questions about a 120-page drug monograph. A consultant advises always loading the full monograph into every API call to avoid missing relevant content.

What is the PRIMARY cost trade-off of this approach?

options.A: Loading the full document increases latency noticeably, affecting user experience but having no direct bearing on API cost.
options.B: The monograph must be re-indexed on every call, incurring a processing fee separate from the token count.
options.C: Loading the full monograph guarantees completeness but is the only viable approach, since shorter contexts risk missing critical passages.
options.D: Paying input token costs for the entire 120-page monograph on every call means charging for the full document even when the user's question concerns only a small section, inflating per-call cost significantly.

items.question:
An insurer's analytics director is designing an API pipeline that scores 10,000 policies daily. Each call sends a 30-page policy document (large input), a 2,000-token system prompt, and receives a 400-token scoring output. Her team is evaluating cost-reduction proposals.

Which TWO proposals would reduce per-call token costs WITHOUT materially degrading scoring quality? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Reduce the system prompt from 2,000 tokens to 200 by removing all explanatory context and keeping only the scoring rubric label.
options.B: Extract only the policy sections relevant to the scoring criteria before sending, rather than sending the full 30-page document every time.
options.C: Increase temperature to reduce the number of generation steps and thereby lower compute cost per output token.
options.D: Implement prompt caching for the system prompt so the fixed 2,000 tokens are served from cache on repeated calls rather than re-processed each time.
options.E: Switch to a lower-cost model tier with no validation of whether scoring accuracy is maintained at the new tier.
